display.title: Red Ivan, Part 2
display.summary_short: Too afraid for his money to send the tzaddik's regards to the robber chief, Beryl struggles home alone, and back at Reb Shmuel's house he finally learns who Red Ivan is.
display.summary_long: After a recap of part 1, Beryl the merchant lies hidden in the inn while the robbers celebrate. Reb Shmuel told him to send regards to the red-bearded Ivan, but Beryl loves his money too much to risk it and stays silent. At dawn he sneaks away and makes his way home on foot, davening with new feeling, keeping negel vasser by his bed even in the forest (with a lesson on why it must be right by the bed), living on berries and stream water, and acting like a madman to escape a beating by peasants. Ragged and unrecognizable, he goes straight to Reb Shmuel, thanks him for the advice about davening that saved his life, and then discovers that all his bank notes are gone. He promises to give tzedakah generously if only he gets them back, and at that moment a man bursts in with the lost packet: Red Ivan himself. Reb Shmuel explains that he was kind to Ivan as a boy, and the robber chief promised to escort home any Jew who sent his regards. Beryl learns his lesson and gives tzedakah with an open hand, and the more he gives, the richer he becomes.
display.lesson: Follow a tzaddik's instructions even when they seem strange, do not love money too much, and give tzedakah generously.
